question: What will you do if you are approaching a pedestrian crossing some distance ahead but are not sure that nobody is standing at it?
option_a: I will stop at the crossing when I reach it.
option_b: I will ease off the accelerator.
option_c: I will drive on without braking.
explanation: The first answer is wrong: in the dark, if you are not sure whether anyone is standing at the crossing, you do not have to stop at every crossing. It is enough to ease off the accelerator and to stop the vehicle if that becomes necessary.

question: What does this sign mean?
option_c: Residential zone.
explanation: "Cyclists" warns of a stretch of road that is often entered or crossed by cyclists and by riders of electric micromobility vehicles.

question: If a driver has comprehensive (KASKO) insurance, is compulsory third party liability insurance also required?
explanation: Compulsory third party liability insurance is always required, even if the car is covered by comprehensive (KASKO) insurance. Note that if you are the owner of the car you do not have to carry these documents with you, but after a road accident you may have to give their details to the other party involved, for example when filling in an accident declaration.

question: In a residential zone, the driver of a lorry must not drive faster than:
option_c: 60 km/h.
option_d: 40 km/h.
explanation: In a residential zone it is prohibited to drive faster than 20 km/h.

question: Is a combine harvester allowed to drive on a motorway?
option_b: It is allowed during the day.
option_c: It is prohibited.
explanation: On roads marked with the signs "Motorway" or "Road for Motor Vehicles" the following are prohibited: pedestrians, driving animal-drawn vehicles, driving or herding animals or birds, horse riding, and the movement of bicycles, electric micromobility vehicles, mopeds, quadricycles of all kinds and all other vehicles, except cars, motorcycles, tricycles, and motorcycles and cars with trailers, provided that the maximum design speed of these motor vehicles, or their speed given their technical condition, is at least 60 km/h.

question: Is it allowed to carry people in the body of a lorry?
option_a: It is allowed if the body has been adapted accordingly and seats have been fitted.
option_b: It is allowed for people accompanying the load.
option_c: It is prohibited, except for passengers carried for the needs of the national defence system.
explanation: Passengers may be carried only in vehicles intended for that purpose (or specially adapted for it) and only in the places designed for passengers. Carrying passengers in the body of a lorry is prohibited, except for passengers carried for the needs of the national defence system, where the body has been adapted for carrying passengers.

question: What does this road sign mean?
option_a: A parking space for electric vehicles, for use only while they are charging.
explanation: Road sign 854, "Electric vehicles". It indicates that the parking space is for electric vehicles to stand in only while they are being charged.

question: What is an intersection of carriageways?
option_a: It is the area bounded by the lines imagined as extensions of the outer edges of the intersecting carriageways.
option_b: It is the area bounded by imaginary lines joining the outer edges of the pavements or shoulders.
explanation: An intersection of carriageways (hereinafter — carriageway intersection) is the area bounded by the straight lines imagined as extensions of the outer edges of the intersecting carriageways, regardless of whether those edges are widened or rounded.

question: In how many rows are cars allowed to stop and stand on the carriageway?
option_c: In three rows.
explanation: Vehicles are allowed to stop and stand on the carriageway in one row only.

question: Is it allowed to pass a car that has been forced to stop in this way?
explanation: Solid road marking lines may be crossed in the exceptional case where it is impossible to continue without changing lane because of a stationary obstruction on the carriageway (a fallen tree, a road accident, a vehicle forced to stop or parked where it should not be, or other stationary objects that make movement impossible), provided that it is safe to do so and other road users are not obstructed.

question: What do these road signs mean?
option_a: Standing is prohibited for 20 m ahead on the side of the road where the signs are placed.
option_b: Standing is prohibited beyond 20 m on the side of the road where the signs are placed.
explanation:
Road sign 333 — No standing (vehicles are prohibited from standing on the side of the road where the sign is. It does not apply to vehicles marked with the "Disabled person" distinguishing sign or with a disabled person's parking card, nor to taxis with the taximeter switched on. If it is used together with marking line 1.9, it applies until the end of that line).
Road sign 806 — Zone of validity ahead (indicates the length of the zone beyond the sign in which the dangerous section of road, or the other road signs it is used with, apply).

question: Is it allowed to pass vehicles travelling in the same direction on their right while driving in a deceleration or acceleration lane?
option_a: It is prohibited in all cases.
option_b: It is allowed only for vehicles that are turning left or making a U-turn.
option_c: It is allowed if you do not obstruct traffic.
option_d: It is allowed only for vehicles travelling slower than 30 km/h.
explanation: Vehicles (except bicycles and electric micromobility vehicles) are prohibited from passing vehicles travelling in the same direction on their right (except for the permitted passing on the right of vehicles that are turning left or making a U-turn) while driving on the shoulder or in a deceleration or acceleration lane. Slower vehicles travelling in the same direction should be passed on the left.

question: When taking part in traffic, drivers of bicycles and of other vehicles classed as powered cycles (electric scooters, electric self-balancing vehicles and similar, with a speed of up to 25 km/h and a power of up to 1 kW) must follow the Road Traffic Rules intended for:
option_c: drivers of motor vehicles.
explanation: The requirements laid down in the Rules for cyclists, together with the road signs and road markings, also apply to drivers of powered cycles.

question: What does a white arrow-shaped traffic light signal on a black background mean?
option_a: That you may only go straight ahead.
option_b: It warns that this street is one-way.
option_c: It warns that you must follow the road signs.
option_d: It permits scheduled public transport to proceed in the indicated direction.

question: Which group of road signs does this sign belong to?
option_c: Vehicle distinguishing and information signs.
option_d: Warning signs.
explanation: In buses fitted with seat belts, an information sign "Fasten your seat belt" must be shown in front of every seat, or in a visible place on or beside the bus seat. The sign is blue and white, the diameter of its circle is 60 mm and the width of the white border is 3 mm.

question: How must vehicles travel if the carriageway is divided into lanes by marking lines?
option_a: Not necessarily in the lanes, if a lane is not wide enough.
option_b: Not necessarily in the lanes, if there are no other vehicles about.
option_c: Only in those lanes. Driving onto a broken marking line is allowed only when changing lanes.
explanation: If the carriageway is divided into lanes by road markings and/or road signs, vehicles must travel in those lanes. Driving onto broken road marking lines is allowed only when changing to another lane; solid road marking lines may be crossed only in the cases set out in Annex 3 to the Rules. Where a solid marking line (single or double) separates the lanes of opposing directions, the driver must keep to the right of it. Solid road marking lines and directional islands may also be crossed in the exceptional case where it is impossible to continue without changing lane because of a stationary obstruction on the carriageway (a fallen tree, a road accident, a vehicle forced to stop or parked where it should not be, or other stationary objects that make movement impossible), provided that it is safe to do so and other road users are not obstructed.

question: What must you do if you are forced to stop on an unlit stretch of road in the dark, or in poor visibility, with the side lights and brake lights out of order?
option_a: Turn the vehicle around and switch on the dipped headlights.
option_b: If the car cannot be parked off the road — switch on the hazard warning lights, and if there are none or they are out of order, place a warning triangle.
option_c: Mark the car with brightly coloured flags.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules, clause 92. If a vehicle has no hazard warning lights or they are out of order and it is forced to stop where stopping or standing is prohibited, or after a road accident, and also if it is forced to stop where other road users would see the stopped vehicle less than 100 m away, the driver of a motor vehicle (except a moped or a motorcycle without a sidecar), a tractor or a self-propelled machine must immediately place a warning triangle facing the direction of oncoming traffic on that side of the carriageway: in built-up areas no closer than 25 m, and outside built-up areas no closer than 50 m from the stopped vehicle. If at least one rear side light fails while driving in the dark or in poor visibility and the hazard warning lights do not work, a warning triangle must be fixed to the rear of the vehicle in order to continue.

Road Traffic Rules, clause 151. A driver forced to stop where stopping (standing) is prohibited must switch on the hazard warning lights, if fitted, and/or place a warning triangle as set out in clause 92 of the Rules, and remove the vehicle from the road as quickly as possible. If you wish to stop on an unlit stretch of road in the dark or in poor visibility and there are no hazard warning lights or they are out of order, the vehicle must be parked off the road. If that cannot be done, the place must be marked as set out in clause 92 of the Rules.

question: In what order will the cars go?
option_c: Blue, yellow, red.
explanation: Because this is a junction of equal-priority roads, drivers must follow the rules for crossing such junctions. The blue car goes first, because when turning left at a junction of equal-priority roads the yellow car must give way to the blue car coming from the opposite direction and going straight ahead. The yellow car goes second, because once it has entered the junction there is no longer an obstacle on its right. The red car goes last, because its obstacle on the right was the yellow car.

question: The silver car is pulling out of a parking space. Which car will have priority?
explanation: Before pulling out of the parking space the silver car must make sure that it will not obstruct other road users and, in this case, must give way to the yellow car.

question: Is it allowed to turn left in the direction shown on this two-way road?
explanation: The road sign "Ahead only". Only straight ahead is allowed. A sign placed at the beginning of a section of road applies as far as the nearest junction and does not prohibit turning right in order to enter premises beside the road. A sign placed before a junction applies only at the carriageway intersection before which it is placed. The requirements of the sign do not apply to scheduled public transport.

question: This sign prohibits:
option_a: the movement of lorries and combinations of vehicles with a mass over 3.5 t, 3 km further on.
option_b: the movement of all vehicles 3 km further on.
option_c: the movement of lorries with a mass over 3.5 t for 3 kilometres from the sign.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 304. Road sign "No lorries". It is prohibited to drive lorries and combinations of vehicles whose maximum authorised mass exceeds 3.5 t or exceeds the mass shown on the sign, and also tractors and self-propelled machines, except vehicles serving premises in the area.
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, plate 801. Plate "Distance to object". It indicates the direction of, and the distance to, an object or the start of a dangerous section of road. The direction of the object (section) shown on the plate is straight ahead.

question: Is it allowed to stop on the shoulder at this spot?
explanation: A sign prohibiting stopping and standing applies only as far as the end of the built-up area. In this situation, therefore, the car is allowed to stand like this.

question: Which driver must give way in this situation on a two-way road?
explanation: Because this stretch of road is marked with a broken road marking line, the driver of the green car may overtake and has priority. The marking line tells us that this is not a junction but an entrance to a yard or premises.

question: Which vehicles are allowed to stand in the parking space marked by this road sign?
option_a: Vehicles marked with the "Disabled person" distinguishing sign.
option_c: Vehicles serving premises in the area.
option_d: Scheduled public transport.
explanation: "Reserved parking space". A parking space where vehicles may stand only with special permits. Permits that are not electronic are displayed behind the windscreen.

question: When is it most appropriate for the driver of an overtaking car to return to the right-hand lane?
option_b: After driving more than 100 m past the overtaken car.
option_c: When the driver of the overtaking car can see the overtaken car in the rear-view mirror.

question: In what order will the vehicles cross the junction (the white car has blue and red beacons and its siren switched on)?
option_a: Emergency vehicle, red car, blue car, yellow car.
option_b: Emergency vehicle, blue car, red car, yellow car.
option_c: Emergency vehicle, blue car, yellow car, red car.
option_d: Emergency vehicle, yellow car, blue car, red car.
explanation: This is a junction of equal-priority roads, so drivers must give way to vehicles approaching from the right if their paths cross. Because the white car has blue and red beacons and a siren switched on, it has priority and goes first. The remaining cars then follow the give-way-to-the-right rule. The red car crosses second, because once the white car has passed it no longer has an obstacle on its right. The blue car goes next, because once the red car has passed there is no longer an obstacle on its right, and finally the yellow car goes.

question: What does this road sign indicate?
option_a: It recommends driving no faster than 40 km/h beyond the sign.
option_b: It prohibits driving faster than 40 km/h on all roads in the area beyond the sign.
option_c: It prohibits driving faster than 40 km/h only as far as the nearest junction.
explanation: "Speed limit zone". On all roads in the area beyond the sign it is prohibited to drive faster (in km/h) than shown on the sign. Where a time is given, the sign applies only during that time.

question: Is it compulsory to stop at the STOP line when turning right in this situation?
explanation: You must stop only where a plate with a green arrow on a white background is fitted. Here there is an additional signal section with a green arrow to the right, so you do not have to stop.

question: What do this road sign and the plates indicate?
option_a: The bends will start in 400 m and continue for 100 m.
option_b: The bends will start in 100 m and continue for 400 m.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 116. "Bends". A section of road with bends of small radius or limited visibility. The first bend is to the left/right.
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, plate 805. "Zone of validity ahead". It indicates the length of the zone beyond the sign in which the dangerous section of road, or the other road signs it is used with, apply.
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, plate 801. "Distance to object". It indicates the direction of, and the distance to, an object or the start of a dangerous section of road. The direction of the object (section) shown on the plate is straight ahead.

question: What speed is the driver of a heavy quadricycle allowed to drive at on the stretch of road beyond these signs?
option_c: 70 km/h.
explanation:
Outside built-up areas the permitted speeds are:
131.6. quadricycles and heavy quadricycles — no more than 70 km/h;

question: Is the driver of the yellow car allowed to make a U-turn at this junction?
explanation: To make a U-turn, the driver of the yellow car should have moved into the far left-hand lane in good time and turned from there.

question: The police car's siren is switched on. Car "2" will cross the junction:
option_c: Second.
option_d: Last.
explanation:
The police car goes first, because its beacons and siren are switched on, so everyone must give way to it.
Cars 1 and 2 are on the major road and car 4 is on the minor road, so car 4 will go last.
Between cars 1 and 2 the give-way-to-the-right rule applies: car 2 must give way to car 1, because car 1 is on its right.

question: Which group of child seat is intended for children weighing between 22 and 36 kg?
option_c: II

question: What effect does wheel locking have on the braking distance?
option_c: The braking distance gets shorter.
explanation: When a car's wheels lock during braking they lose grip on the road surface. This sliding means that the braking friction becomes lower than when the wheels are still rolling. As a result the car slows down more slowly and the braking distance gets longer. The driver also loses the ability to steer the car, which makes sudden manoeuvres dangerous. Modern vehicles use an ABS system, which prevents the wheels from locking and ensures effective and safe braking.

question: How can you tell while driving whether your car's main beam headlights are switched on?
option_c: By a blue warning light.
option_d: By a red warning light.
explanation: When the main beam headlights are switched on, a blue warning light normally comes on in the instrument panel. This lets the driver see easily that the lights are on, even when they cannot see the beams directly.

question: How long does it take for 1.0 per mille of alcohol to leave the blood?
option_c: 10 hours.
explanation: The body removes about 0.1–0.15 per mille per hour on average. Bringing 1.0 per mille down to 0 can therefore often take about 10 hours if the concentration was high.

question: What will you do in this situation (a trolleybus is standing before the crossing)?
option_a: On reaching the pedestrian crossing you will reduce speed and, seeing no pedestrians, drive on.
option_b: On reaching the pedestrian crossing you will stop and, having made sure there are no pedestrians, drive on.
option_c: You will drive at the same speed as before, paying no attention to the stopped trolleybus.
explanation: In a situation like this, pedestrians walking out from behind the trolleybus may not be visible, so if you drive on without stopping you could knock them down. You must therefore stop at the crossing and drive on only after letting the pedestrians pass or making sure that there are none.

question: Placed in a built-up area, this road sign warns that:
option_a: The dangerous section with bends will start 50–100 m beyond the sign.
option_b: The dangerous section with bends will start immediately beyond the sign.
option_c: The dangerous section with bends will start 150–300 m beyond the sign.
explanation: Outside built-up areas, warning signs 101–137 and 150 are placed 150–300 m before the start of the dangerous section of road, and in built-up areas 50–100 m before it.

question: If a vehicle with its siren and beacons (blue and red) switched on approaches the junction in this situation, the driver of the red car:
option_a: Will drive on without giving way to anyone, because the traffic light is green for them.
option_b: Must give way to the emergency vehicle.
explanation: Road users must give way immediately to approaching emergency vehicles with blue and red (or only blue) beacons and sirens switched on, and to the vehicles they are escorting.

question: What is the maximum speed allowed beyond this sign at 6 o'clock in the morning?
option_c: 60 km/h.
explanation: The road sign applies from 21:00 in the evening until 07:00 in the morning (all night). It therefore applies at 6 o'clock in the morning as well.

question: The driver of which vehicle will cross the junction second?
option_c: The red car.
explanation: The yellow and the red car, both travelling on the major road, must follow the rules for crossing junctions of equal-priority roads in relation to each other. The yellow car therefore goes first, because the red car has an obstacle on its right (the yellow car). The red car goes next, and finally the lorry.

question: When the green traffic light comes on, may you make a U-turn?
option_a: Yes, if you are in the second lane.
explanation: If the road signs and/or road markings allow it, you may turn left or make a U-turn on a general green traffic light, but only after giving way to oncoming cars and to pedestrians and cyclists crossing the road you are turning into.

question: Which driver has priority?
option_a: The driver of the blue car.
option_b: The driver of the red car.
explanation: The give-way-to-the-right rule applies here. The red car has an obstacle on its right, so it goes second.

question: The driver of which car will cross the junction last (the white car is turning left)?
option_a: The driver of the white car.
option_b: The driver of the blue car.
option_c: The driver of the green car.
explanation: The green and the white car are on the major road of equal priority, so the green car goes first, because the white car has an obstacle on its right (that same green car). The white car goes next, and finally the blue car, because it is on the minor road.

question: Is such an overtaking manoeuvre allowed on this stretch of road?
explanation: Because the overtaking manoeuvre is started before the level crossing and takes place on the crossing itself, such overtaking is a breach of the Road Traffic Rules.

question: Which direction indicator will you use when going straight ahead at a junction of equal-priority roads outside a built-up area?
option_c: I will not use any.
explanation: No direction indicator is used when going straight ahead, because the direction of travel is not being changed.

question: What does an area marked with yellow lines at a carriageway intersection mean?
option_a: It marks a place you must not drive into if there is an obstruction in it or beyond it.
option_c: It marks a dangerous section of road.
explanation: An area marked with yellow lines at a carriageway intersection marks a place you must not drive into if there is an obstruction in it or beyond it that would force the driver to stop at the carriageway intersection and obstruct the movement of other vehicles.

question: Is a person working on the road considered to be a pedestrian?
explanation: A person working on the road is a person repairing or maintaining the road or technical traffic control devices, directing and supervising traffic, removing from the road or fencing off a vehicle forced to stop or another obstruction, dealing with the consequences of a road accident or other emergency, carrying out other rescue work, or giving medical assistance to a person injured in a road accident on the road or to another person who needs medical assistance.

question: Novice drivers must mark their car with this distinguishing sign:
option_c: At the front and at the rear.
explanation: Novice drivers must display, on the left-hand side of the rear of the car, a white square distinguishing sign with a green border and a green maple leaf in the middle. The side of the square is between 100 mm and 150 mm long and the width of the border is 1/10 of the length of the side.

question: What does this road marking indicate?
option_a: It indicates that you are approaching a "Stop" line, when it is used together with the "Stop" sign.
option_b: It indicates that you are approaching a place where stopping is compulsory.
option_c: It indicates a place where you must give way to pedestrians.
explanation: The word "STOP" indicates that you are approaching marking line 1.11, when that line is used together with the road sign "Stop".

question: When driving in poor visibility, a driver must choose a speed at which the stopping distance is:
option_a: Shorter than the length of road that can be seen.
option_b: Longer than the length of road that can be seen.
explanation: This makes sure that, on spotting an obstruction, the car will be able to stop safely without going beyond the visible zone.

question: What does this symbol warn about when it lights up on the instrument panel?
option_c: A fault in the anti-lock braking system.
explanation: The ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) symbol lighting up on the instrument panel warns of a fault in the anti-lock braking system. It means the system has detected an error and has switched the ABS function off automatically to avoid the brakes working incorrectly.

question: In which of the following engine states is the battery the only source of energy for the electrical consumers?
option_a: When the crankshaft speed is medium or higher.
option_b: When the engine is not running.
option_c: When the crankshaft speed is low or medium.
explanation: The battery is the only source of energy in ACC (accessory) mode, when the engine is not running.

question: Which wheels does the parking brake act on?
option_c: Both the front and the rear wheels.
option_d: The rear or the front wheels.
explanation: The parking brake acts on the front or the rear wheels, depending on how the car is built. On most cars it acts on the rear wheels, but on some older or special vehicles it may be connected to the front wheels.

question: When entering a roundabout you must always:
option_c: Turn left.
explanation: When entering a roundabout you must always give way to the drivers already travelling on it. Under the Road Traffic Rules you must not signal when entering a roundabout. You must also keep to the marked lanes, obey the road signs controlling the roundabout (for example "Give way") and the traffic lights, and keep to a safe speed.

question: You intend to turn right from an unsurfaced road onto a road with an asphalt surface. What will you do in this situation?
option_a: I will go first, because I have priority.
option_b: I will give way to the car coming from the left.
explanation: Under the Road Traffic Rules, when leaving an unsurfaced road (a gravel, field or forest road) for a surfaced road you must give way, stopping if necessary, and let all vehicles crossing your path pass, because in this case the surfaced road counts as the major road compared with the unsurfaced one.

question: Why must you make sure the indicator is switched off after taking a turn?
option_a: So as not to dazzle other road users.
option_b: So as not to drain the battery.
option_c: So as not to damage the indicator switch (relay).
option_d: So as not to mislead other road users.
explanation: After taking a turn you must make sure the indicator is switched off so that you do not mislead other road users and cause dangerous situations. A false signal can make other drivers wrongly believe that you are turning again or stopping, which creates a hazard.

question: Is it allowed to make a U-turn at this junction at 3 p.m.?
explanation: At this junction there is a road sign showing that you may go straight ahead or turn left. Below the sign is a plate with the times "14–17 h", which means the restriction applies during those hours. Since the sign does not allow a U-turn, you cannot turn round at 3 p.m.

question: Your car has broken down while you were driving on a motorway. You have stopped on the surfaced hard shoulder. Where is the safest place to wait for help?
option_c: In the car.
option_d: In front of the car.
explanation: The safest place to wait for help is behind the crash barrier, on the green verge, well away from the carriageway.

question: What does a broken white line along the middle of the road mean?
option_a: You must watch out for oncoming vehicles.
option_b: It may be crossed only when it is safe to do so.
option_c: Do not overtake.
explanation: A broken white line along the middle of the road marks the lane boundaries for vehicles travelling in the same direction.

question: When may you bring your vehicle to a stop at a carriageway intersection?
option_a: When I am waiting for an opportunity to turn left.
option_b: When I am turning right onto the major road in heavy traffic.
option_c: Never.
explanation: While waiting to turn left you are allowed to stop in order to let oncoming traffic pass.

question: What does this sign mean?
option_c: Ahead only.
explanation: The sign means that you must go straight ahead.

question: What is the maximum speed allowed in a built-up area for a lorry with a maximum authorised mass of 3.5 t towing a trailer?
option_c: 50 km/h
explanation: The sign "Built-up area" (Tytuvėnai) means that you are entering a built-up area and that the rules for built-up areas start to apply. The maximum speed is 50 km/h.

question: Having passed the tests at the state enterprise "Regitra", you may start driving on your own:
option_b: Only once you have received your driving licence.
option_c: If you have a copy of the test report.
explanation: Even though the tests have been passed, you may drive only once you hold the physical licence, because it has to be produced during a check.

question: Is the driver of a car allowed to stop in the right-hand lane of a road marked with this road sign?
explanation: The sign shows that the right-hand lane is reserved for scheduled public transport (buses). The driver of a car may therefore not stop in it, unless additional signs allow it.

question: Is it allowed to carry people in a towed caravan?
explanation: A towed caravan is not intended for carrying people while on the move, so there must be no passengers in it.

question: What will you do when driving up a steep hill in a car with a manual gearbox?
option_a: I will change up to a higher gear.
option_b: I will change down to a lower gear.
option_c: I will stay in the same gear.
explanation: Driving up a steep hill with a manual gearbox calls for a lower gear, because it gives more pulling power and makes it easier for the engine to take the car uphill.

question: A slow-moving vehicle ahead of you is forcing you to reduce your speed considerably. What will you do?
option_a: I will flash my headlights to urge them to go faster.
option_b: I will drive close behind so that I can overtake as soon as possible.
option_c: I will stay behind until an opportunity to overtake safely appears.
explanation: Even if a slow-moving vehicle ahead is holding you up, you must not flash your headlights at it or drive too close. You should keep a safe distance and wait for a moment when overtaking is safe and permitted.

question: You are driving on a motorway. When may you use the left-hand lane?
option_a: Until I have passed the vehicles travelling more slowly in the right-hand lane.
option_b: I may use it all the time, even if the right-hand lane is free.
explanation: On a motorway you should keep as far right as possible; the left-hand lane is for overtaking or passing. Once the manoeuvre is finished you must return to the right-hand lane.

question: During the driving test:
option_a: I will drive very slowly, to impress the examiner.
option_b: I will drive the way I usually do.
explanation: During the driving test there is no need to drive unusually slowly on purpose or to try to impress in any other way. What matters is driving calmly and confidently, following the road traffic rules and the way you are used to driving safely.

question: The traffic controller's arms are lowered. The traffic light at the junction is red. Are you allowed to go straight ahead?
explanation: When traffic at a junction is being directed by a traffic controller, their signals take precedence over the traffic lights. If the controller's arms are lowered and they are standing sideways to you, you are allowed to go straight ahead even though the traffic light is red.

question: What does this road sign mean?
option_b: End of the zone where standing is prohibited.
option_c: End of the zone where stopping is prohibited.
option_d: End of the major road.
explanation: A yellow diamond means a major road, and when it is crossed out with diagonal black lines it shows that the major road ends. As you drive on you must watch the other signs carefully and follow the priority rules at junctions.

question: You intend to turn right at the junction. What will you do in this situation?
option_a: I will turn in front of the cyclist, because I have priority.
option_b: I will let the cyclist going straight ahead pass and then turn.
explanation: When turning right you must give way to a cyclist going straight ahead in the same direction. Only once you have let them pass can you make the turn safely.

question: In what order will the vehicles cross the junction (the white car has a green traffic light)?
option_a: The brown car together with the green one, then the white one.
option_c: White, then the brown car together with the green one.
explanation: The green traffic light is showing for all three cars. The white car will cross the junction first, because the brown and the green car, turning left, must give way to cars turning right.

question: Holders of a certificate issued by an educational establishment are allowed to ride a bicycle on the road from the age of:
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, clause 55. Riding a bicycle on the carriageway is allowed for people aged at least 14, and for people aged at least 12 who have completed the training course set by the Ministry of Education, Science and Sport of the Republic of Lithuania and hold a certificate issued by their school. Under the supervision of an adult, riding a bicycle on the carriageway is allowed from the age of 8. In a residential zone there is no age limit for cyclists.

question: Does the driver of the white car have priority (it is turning left)?
explanation: Both cars are on the major road, so between themselves they follow the give-way-to-the-right rule. The blue car has no obstacle on its right, so it goes first. The white car therefore does not have priority in this case.

question: Which drivers, travelling in the directions of the arrows, must give way to other road users?
option_c: The blue car.
option_d: The cyclist.
explanation: The driver of the blue car is coming out of a car park (yard), so they must give way to all vehicles on the road they are entering.

question: In what order will the vehicles cross the junction (the black car has amber beacons switched on, the white car is turning left)?
option_a: The white and the blue car together, then the black one.
option_c: Blue, white, black.
option_d: Black, blue, white.
explanation: The white and the blue car go first, because both are on the major road and their paths do not cross. The black car goes last, because it is coming from the minor road. Amber beacons do not give priority.

question: What does this sign prohibit?
option_a: Vehicles standing on even days of the month on the side where this sign is.
option_b: Vehicles standing on odd days of the week on the side where this sign is.
explanation: The even days of the month are the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and so on. An even day of the month becomes an odd one at 24:00.

question: Who is allowed to cross a level crossing when its red light is on?
option_a: Drivers of emergency vehicles travelling on the road with blue and red (or only blue) beacons and sirens switched on.
option_b: Cars with amber beacons switched on.
option_c: Road maintenance vehicles.
option_d: All vehicles are prohibited from proceeding.
explanation: Emergency service crews decide for themselves when it is safe to cross a level crossing and when it is not.

question: The plate indicates that:
option_a: A section marked in this way is often slippery because of ice or snow.
option_b: The air temperature on this section is low.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, plate 848. "Icy road". A section marked in this way is often slippery because of ice or snow.

question: Who must give way?
explanation: When approaching a place where the carriageway has to be crossed, a cyclist must in all cases reduce speed and may continue only after making sure that it is safe to do so. In addition, a cyclist wishing to cross the carriageway where traffic is not controlled must give way to vehicles travelling on the carriageway, except when crossing exits from premises beside the road, from a residential zone, a yard or a car park, and when crossing a carriageway into which other drivers are turning.

question: In which cases is it allowed to pass this road sign?
option_a: It is not allowed in any case.
option_b: It is allowed if the mass of your vehicle, including the trailer and the load, is not greater than the mass shown on the sign.
option_c: It is always allowed, only at a safe speed.
option_d: It is allowed if the load on any one axle does not exceed the figure shown on the sign.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 314. "Mass limit". It is prohibited to drive vehicles, or combinations of vehicles, whose mass with or without a load is greater than the mass shown on the sign.

question: What is the maximum speed beyond this road sign, on a road with an asphalt surface (not an expressway or a motorway), for a driver with less than 2 years of driving experience?
option_c: 60 km/h.
option_d: 50 km/h.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules, clause 131. Outside built-up areas the permitted speeds are:
131.2. category A1, A2, A or B vehicles driven by novice drivers, by learner drivers or by people taking the practical driving test, and buses (including school buses): on motorways no more than 100 km/h, on expressways no more than 90 km/h, on roads with an asphalt or concrete surface no more than 80 km/h, and on other roads no more than 70 km/h;
Law on Road Traffic Safety, Article 2. Main definitions used in this Law:
31. Learner — a person who is learning to drive a vehicle in the prescribed manner.
52. Novice driver — a person who has acquired the right to drive a category A, A1, A2, B or B1 motor vehicle and has less than two years of driving experience.

question: In what order will the cars cross the junction?
option_b: The red car together with the blue one, then the yellow one.
option_c: Yellow, then the red car together with the blue one.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, clause 154. At a junction of roads of unequal priority, a driver travelling on the minor road must give way to vehicles approaching the junction on the major road.

question: Who has priority at the junction?
option_a: The driver of the blue car.
explanation: At the junction we can see road signs and a traffic light, but under the road traffic rules the traffic light takes precedence over the road signs. The traffic light is showing a green signal allowing movement in the directions indicated. The cyclist therefore follows the traffic light and crosses the junction first. The car is turning left, so it must give way to the cyclist turning right (Road Traffic Rules, clause 157).

question: Is it allowed to make a U-turn in this situation?
explanation: After turning round, the car would end up in lane A, where it is not allowed to drive.

question: When does a road sign used together with this supplementary plate apply?
option_a: When the road surface is dry.
option_b: When the road surface is damp (wet).
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, plate 845 "Wet surface". It indicates that the sign the plate is used with applies when the surface of the carriageway is damp (wet).

question: What does a horizontal solid black line mark?
option_a: It marks the side surfaces of barriers on sharp bends, steep descents and other dangerous sections.
option_b: It marks signalling devices placed on central reservations or safety islands.
option_c: It marks kerbs on dangerous sections and raised safety islands.
option_d: It marks the side surfaces of barriers on other sections of road.
explanation: A horizontal solid black line marks the side surfaces of barriers on other sections of road.

question: What do horizontal black and white bands mark?
option_a: They mark road structures that are a hazard to moving vehicles.
option_b: They mark the lower edge of the structures of bridges, flyovers and tunnels.
option_c: They mark signalling devices placed on central reservations or safety islands.
option_d: They mark marker posts, gates and barrier supports.
explanation: Horizontal black and white bands mark signalling devices placed on central reservations or safety islands.

question: What will you do when you are approaching a bend with limited visibility?
option_a: I will drive on without changing speed.
option_b: I will ease off the accelerator.
option_c: I will brake.
explanation: When approaching a bend a driver must allow for the fact that it may be sharper than expected, and must therefore choose a safe speed and a suitable position on the road so as not to run into the oncoming lane. A safe speed depends on all the circumstances: the weather, the condition of the road and of the vehicle, and also the driver's experience and how they feel.

question: What do vertical diagonal black and white bands on road structures mark?
option_a: They mark road structures that are a hazard to moving vehicles.
option_b: They mark the lower edge of the structures of bridges, flyovers and tunnels.
option_c: They mark signalling devices placed on central reservations or safety islands.
option_d: They mark marker posts, gates and barrier supports.
explanation: Diagonal black and white bands mark the vertical elements of road structures (bridges, flyover supports, the end sections of barriers and so on) where those elements are a hazard to moving vehicles, and they also mark the supports of direction signs Nos 407–409 on central reservations and at road forks.

question: In which directions is movement allowed?
option_c: Right only.
option_d: In all the directions shown.
explanation: Traffic controller's arms stretched out to the sides or lowered: from the chest side and the back side, all vehicles and pedestrians are prohibited from moving.

question: Does the pavement form part of the definition of a road?
explanation: A road is a strip of the surface of the ground or of a structure that is intended and used for traffic, over its full width, including the carriageway of the road (hereinafter — the carriageway), junctions, pavements, shoulders, footpaths and cycle tracks, and central reservations.

question: Must the driver signal when turning left in this situation?
explanation: A driver must give warning with the direction indicators for the appropriate direction, or by hand if there are no indicators or they are out of order: before moving off and before stopping; before changing lanes, before starting and before finishing an overtake, before starting and before finishing passing an obstruction, before turning right or left, before making a U-turn, and when leaving a roundabout.

question: Which vehicle will cross the junction first?
explanation:
At a junction of roads of unequal priority, a driver travelling on the minor road must give way to vehicles approaching the junction on the major road. If the direction of the major road changes at the junction, drivers travelling on the major road must follow the rules for crossing junctions of equal-priority roads in relation to each other. Drivers travelling on the minor roads must follow those same rules in relation to each other.

Cars 3 and 4 are on the major road. Car 3 continues along the major road while car 4 wants to leave it, so car 3 crosses the junction first and car 4 gives way to it (obstacle on the right). Car 1 goes next, since it is an obstacle on the right for car 2 — so car 2 goes last.

question: What will you do in this situation?
option_a: Reduce your speed to 10 km/h so that the children have time to move away.
option_c: Stop, switch on the hazard warning lights, and drive on only once the children have left the carriageway.
explanation: The horn must not be used, so that the children are not startled and do not end up under the wheels of another car. In such a case you should stop and switch on the hazard warning lights (other drivers will not be able to overtake you, because crossing the solid line is prohibited).

question: A driver who, when the amber traffic light comes on or the traffic controller raises their arm, could only stop by braking sharply is allowed to:
option_c: Brake sharply in any case.
explanation: A driver who, when the amber (or white horizontal bar) traffic light comes on or the traffic controller raises their arm, could stop at the places set out in clause 165 of the Rules only by braking sharply is allowed to drive on.

question: Which lane may moped riders use?
option_b: Only the first lane from the right-hand edge of the carriageway.
option_c: Both the first and the second lane from the right-hand edge of the carriageway.
option_d: Mopeds are prohibited from using traffic lanes.
explanation: Riders of mopeds and drivers of light quadricycles must use only the first lane from the right-hand edge of the carriageway, keeping as close as possible to its right-hand edge, except when they need to turn left, make a U-turn, pass an obstruction, go straight ahead where the first lane allows only a right turn, or stop or stand on a one-way road.

question: Is a pedestrian allowed to cross a road with a central reservation?
explanation: Pedestrians are prohibited from crossing the carriageway at places where there are vehicle or pedestrian barriers and, in built-up areas, also where there is a central reservation (except at pedestrian crossings and junctions).

question: May you drive on if the coupling device between the vehicle and the trailer has failed?
explanation: It is prohibited to drive a motor vehicle, a tractor or a self-propelled machine if: the service brake does not work (the driver cannot stop the vehicle with it); the steering mechanism does not work (the driver cannot control the vehicle with it); the coupling device between the vehicle and the trailer is faulty; the windscreen wiper on the driver's side does not work in rain, snow or fog; in the dark or in poor visibility no front left lamp (dipped beam or fog lamp) is lit, or, if at least one rear side light has failed, the hazard warning lights do not work (are not switched on) or no warning triangle is fixed to the rear of the vehicle.

question: Must a vehicle being used for work on the road switch on its amber beacons if it is not obstructing traffic?
explanation:
A vehicle's amber beacon must be switched on when traffic is being obstructed (because the vehicle, with or without a load, is larger than permitted, when working on the road, when stopped or standing, when moving slowly, when escorting an organised group of cyclists, or when carrying dangerous goods). A lit amber beacon does not give priority; it only draws attention and warns other road users of a possible hazard. Drivers of vehicles with amber beacons switched on must make sure, while driving, standing and/or carrying out work, that this does not endanger road safety.

When road infrastructure or environmental maintenance work is being carried out on a contractual basis and under the conditions set by the road owner, a vehicle with an amber beacon switched on that is needed to carry out the work at that place may drive on grass verges, pavements, footpaths and/or cycle tracks, cycle lanes, central reservations, embankment or cutting slopes and ditches, and may also stop or stand in those places.

question: The traffic light or the traffic controller's signals prohibit crossing the pedestrian crossing. Where must you stop?
option_a: No closer than 3 metres before the crossing.
option_b: No closer than 5 metres before the crossing.
option_c: Before the "Stop" sign or the stop line, or the traffic light, and if there are none — before the controlled pedestrian crossing.
explanation: If the traffic light or the traffic controller's signals prohibit movement, the driver must stop before the "Stop line" road sign and/or the "Stop" line, or the traffic light, and if there are none — before the controlled pedestrian crossing. Drivers who, when the amber (or white horizontal bar) traffic light comes on or the traffic controller raises their arm, could stop at those places only by braking sharply are allowed to drive on.

question: Does incorrect wheel alignment increase fuel consumption?
explanation: Incorrect wheel alignment increases rolling resistance, and fuel consumption therefore rises.

question: Which road sign means a vehicle repair workshop?
explanation:
1. Mandatory road sign. Stop (a stopping place for scheduled public transport).

2. Service road sign. Rural tourism homestead.

3. Service road sign. Bus station (a place for serving passengers travelling on scheduled local, long-distance and international routes).

4. Service road sign. Workshop (a vehicle repair workshop).

question: A tyre is marked 195/55 R15. What does the number 15 indicate?
option_b: The ratio of the tyre's height to its width.
option_c: The diameter of the rim.
option_d: The tyre's permitted load index.
explanation:
"R" means that the tyre is radial (in practice cross-ply tyres are sometimes used as well; radial tyres differ from cross-ply ones in their construction and radial tyres are the better ones. Modern cars use radial tyres. Cross-ply tyres are used on slow-moving vehicles such as agricultural machinery and special vehicles). "195" is the width of the tyre and "55" is its height.

"15" means that the diameter of the tyre is 15 inches (the wheel diameter of cars can be from 12 to 17 inches, while the wheels of heavier vehicles reach 25 inches or more).

"M+S" means that the tyre can also be used in winter.

"TUBELESS" means that the tyre has no inner tube (because of the way it is built, the tyre fits tightly against the rim and holds the air inside itself. In tyres with a tube, an inner tube is fitted inside the tyre and is filled with air, giving the tyre its proper shape).

question: Why is it dangerous to drive fast on an asphalt road in heavy rain?
option_b: Water will get onto the engine and it will cut out.
option_c: Aquaplaning (a wedge of water) may occur and the car will become uncontrollable.
explanation: It is dangerous to drive at high speed on an asphalt road in heavy rain, because a wedge of water (aquaplaning) forms under the car's wheels and the car becomes hard to control. The wedge of water is a thin gap of water between the carriageway and the tyre. It forms because of high speed and worn tyre tread.

question: What must the driver on whose side the obstruction lies do if it is difficult to pass an oncoming vehicle?
option_a: They must give way to the oncoming vehicle.
option_b: Speed up and pass the obstruction, because they have priority.
explanation: If it is difficult to pass an oncoming vehicle, the driver on whose side the obstruction lies must give way.

question: Are pedestrians allowed to walk along the edge of the carriageway?
option_a: It is allowed in two rows, facing the direction of traffic.
option_b: It is allowed, if there is no pavement, footpath or shoulder or they cannot be used, in single file facing the direction of traffic.
option_c: It is prohibited.
option_d: It is allowed, if there is no pavement, footpath or shoulder or they cannot be used, in single file in the same direction as the traffic.
explanation: Pedestrians must use pavements, footpaths, or shared footpaths and cycle tracks (on the side intended for pedestrians), and where there are none — the shoulder. If there is no pavement, footpath, shared footpath and cycle track or shoulder, or they cannot be used, walking in single file along the edge of the carriageway is allowed. Pedestrians moving along the shoulder or the edge of the carriageway, and those using roller skates, skateboards or non-powered scooters on the shoulder, must move facing the direction of traffic.

question: How must a load be marked if it projects 0.2 m beyond the sides of the vehicle?
option_a: With squares carrying alternating reflective diagonal white and red stripes.
option_c: No marking is needed.
option_d: With squares carrying alternating reflective diagonal white and orange stripes.
explanation:
If a load projects more than 1 m beyond the vehicle at the front or the rear, or if its side edge projects at all beyond the side of the vehicle, it must be marked as set out in Annex 4 to the Rules.

The outermost points of a load projecting more than 1 m beyond the vehicle at the front or the rear, or projecting at all to the side, and the outer points of vehicles wider than 2.6 m, must be marked with distinguishing signs — squares with 400 mm sides carrying alternating reflective diagonal white and red stripes 50 mm wide. These signs must be fixed to the vehicle no lower than 0.4 m and no higher than 1.6 m above the ground. In the dark or in poor visibility, lamps must be lit at those points on the vehicle — white at the front, amber at the sides and red at the rear.

question: What is the best way to brake on a slippery road?
option_a: Brake in pulses, with frequent presses of the service brake, without locking the wheels and without disengaging the clutch and the gear.
option_b: Disengage the gear and brake with the parking (hand) brake.
explanation:
A car is more stable when it is driven in gear, because this allows the engine's torque to be controlled more effectively. When the engine is running it passes turning force through the gearbox, which changes the speed and the torque. In gear, the engine works at a steady torque, which makes it easier to control the car's stability and its driving force. Using the gears effectively also reduces the risk of skidding, especially in difficult weather or when you need to stop quickly. It is therefore recommended to drive in gear and to use the gear change properly, so that driving stays safe and predictable.

With the clutch and the gear still engaged the car is more stable, because the driven wheels meet resistance from the engine and so help to brake and steady the car.

When braking with intermittent presses of the brake pedal the car does not lose grip on the road surface and stays more stable than when the wheels are locked completely, because then the wheels start to slide and the car becomes uncontrollable.

question: On which side of the carriageway may people on roller skates, skateboards or non-powered scooters travel?
option_a: Along the edge of the carriageway in the direction of traffic.
option_b: Along the edge of the carriageway facing the direction of traffic.
option_c: It is prohibited, except in residential zones.
explanation: Pedestrians are prohibited from using roller skates, skateboards or non-powered scooters on the carriageway, except in a residential zone.

question: Traffic in the picture is controlled by traffic lights. The pedestrian must:
option_b: Wait on the safety island until the traffic light allows them to continue.
option_c: Turn round and go back.
explanation: Pedestrians must not linger or stand about on the carriageway. Those who have not managed to cross the carriageway must wait on a safety island or on the marked or imaginary line separating the traffic flows of opposing directions. They may finish crossing the carriageway only after making sure that it is safe to do so.

question: When must a cyclist crossing the point where a cycle track meets a road give way to other vehicles?
option_b: They do not have to give way, because they have priority.
option_c: Where the cycle track meets the road away from a junction and traffic is not controlled.
option_d: When a vehicle is approaching from the right.
explanation: A cyclist intending to cross the carriageway where traffic is not controlled, or where there are no road signs establishing priority, must give way to vehicles travelling on the carriageway, except when crossing exits from premises beside the road, from a residential zone, a yard or a car park, and when crossing a carriageway into which other drivers are turning.

question: At what distance before the start of their zone of validity are the road signs shown placed in a built-up area?
explanation: The dangerous section of road marked by warning signs Nos 101–137, 150 and 151 starts 50–100 m beyond the place where the warning sign is installed in a built-up area, and 150–300 m beyond it outside a built-up area. If those warning signs are installed together with the supplementary plate "Distance to object", the dangerous section starts at the distance given on that plate. If they are installed together with the supplementary plate "Zone of validity ahead", that plate indicates the length of the dangerous section, which starts 50–100 m beyond the warning sign in built-up areas and 150–300 m beyond it outside built-up areas.

question: At what distance from a bus stop is it prohibited to leave a motor vehicle standing if it obstructs scheduled public transport?
explanation: Stopping and standing are prohibited in the stopping bays of scheduled public transport and closer than 15 m to them (where there is no bay — closer than 15 m to the "Stop" road sign), if this would obstruct the movement of scheduled public transport; standing is prohibited within the zone of validity of the "Taxi rank" road sign.

question: Is it allowed to cross the solid road marking line in this situation?
explanation:
If the requirements of a road sign and of the road markings differ, the road sign must be followed. In this case, following the road sign, the obstruction must be passed on the left, even though the narrow solid white line says otherwise.

A narrow solid line separates traffic flows of opposing directions and prohibits driving in the oncoming lane on the marked section of road; it marks the edges of lanes, sections of the carriageway that must not be entered, the boundaries of parking spaces and the edge of the carriageway; where road sign No 413 "Footpath and cycle track" is used, it separates the part of the track intended for cyclists from the part intended for pedestrians. Crossing this line is prohibited, except where it marks the edge of the carriageway or a parking space.

question: Must a driver wear a seat belt when reversing in a built-up area?
explanation: In built-up areas a driver is allowed not to wear a seat belt when reversing or in car parks.

question: When does the centrifugal force decrease in a turn?
option_c: When the radius of the turn is reduced.
explanation: The centrifugal force acting on a car is greater in a sharp turn. In a sharp turn the centrifugal force will be smaller if the turn is taken slowly.

question: If the speed increases from 15 km/h to 45 km/h, the braking distance increases:
option_c: Nine times.
option_d: Twelve times.
explanation: The higher the speed, the longer the braking distance (the relationship is a square one): that is, if you double the speed, the braking distance becomes four times longer.

question: Which driver is breaking the Road Traffic Rules in the situation shown (the yellow and the black car are on a two-way road)?
option_a: The driver of the black car.
option_b: The driver of the yellow car.
option_c: The driver of the blue car.
explanation: Overtaking at junctions is prohibited.

question: A lorry with a maximum authorised mass of 3 t is allowed to go:
option_c: Left and make a U-turn.
explanation: Lorries of up to 3.5 tonnes are treated as cars (category B).

question: What should you do if the right-hand wheels of the car drift off the asphalt onto a gravel shoulder?
option_a: Without braking, steer the car back onto the carriageway by turning the steering wheel slowly to the left.
option_b: Braking sharply, steer the car back onto the carriageway.
option_c: Stop and then move off again.
explanation: In this case the car can be brought back onto the carriageway safely without braking, by turning the steering wheel slowly to the left. If you tried to bring the car back onto the carriageway without braking but by turning the steering wheel sharply to the left, the increased centrifugal force could make the car skid or roll over. Braking sharply in this situation could take the car off its path, because during braking the grip of the right-hand wheels on the shoulder would be much lower than the grip of the left-hand wheels on the asphalt.

question: Is it allowed to stop on the shoulder at this spot?
explanation: A sign prohibiting stopping and standing applies only as far as the end of the built-up area. In this situation, therefore, the car is allowed to stand like this.

question: Which driver has priority? The driver of the blue car is making a U-turn at the junction.
option_a: The driver of the yellow car.
option_b: The driver of the blue car.
explanation: In this case the drivers of the blue and the yellow car are in an equal position, because they are at a junction of equal-priority roads. The blue car is making a U-turn at the junction, so before it finishes turning round an obstacle appears on its right — the yellow car — and the blue car must therefore give way to the yellow one.

question: Who is allowed to stop beyond these road signs in the situation shown (the lane is marked with the letter "A")?
option_c: Scheduled public transport.
explanation: Scheduled public transport is allowed to stop, but not to stand. Other vehicles may not stop beyond the signs, because they are prohibited from entering the lane for scheduled public transport marked with the letter A, unless they are about to turn right.

question: In which directions is a car allowed to go in the situation shown?
option_c: Driving on is prohibited.
explanation: The sign with its supplementary plate shows that motor vehicles are prohibited from using the street to the left. A car may therefore go straight ahead.

question: Is it allowed to carry people in a car that is being towed?
explanation: Carrying people in a car that is being towed is prohibited. Only a vehicle without passengers may be towed (except the driver, if that is needed to control the vehicle).

question: The road sign indicates:
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 556. Road sign "End of road for motor vehicles". The end of the road on which the traffic rules laid down for expressways apply.

question: Is it allowed to drive through a lit tunnel during the day with only the daytime running lights switched on?
explanation: Driving through a tunnel, even a lit one, counts as driving in poor visibility. You must therefore switch on the dipped beam headlights in a tunnel; daytime running lights are not enough. Daytime running lights (for example the LEDs on modern cars) and dipped beam headlights are not the same thing.

question: Does a road marking that allows a left turn from the far left lane also allow a U-turn?
option_c: Yes, but only on working days.
option_d: The Road Traffic Rules do not define this.
explanation:
Road markings:
1.16. Arrows show the directions of travel permitted in a lane. A dead-end symbol warns that turning into the nearest carriageway is prohibited. A marking that allows a left turn from the far left lane also allows a U-turn.

question: What does this road sign mean?
option_c: Parking zone.
explanation: Road sign 561 — "Low emission zone". An area of a city, established by the municipal council, in which on all roads beyond the sign the movement of motor vehicles, tractors and self-propelled machines is restricted or completely prohibited, except for zero-emission vehicles.

question: What does the road sign shown prohibit?
option_a: Driving more slowly than the speed shown.
option_b: Driving faster than the speed shown.
option_c: Driving faster than the speed shown, except for scheduled public transport.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 329. Road sign "Speed limit". It is prohibited to drive faster (in km/h) than shown on the sign.

question: This road sign indicates:
option_a: The direction of travel on roads where roadworks are being carried out.
option_b: The number of lanes and the directions of travel in each lane.
explanation: The number of arrows drawn on this sign does not depend on the number of traffic lanes.

question: In what order will the cars cross the junction?
option_c: Green, red, blue.
option_d: Blue, red, green.
explanation: At this junction of equal-priority roads the green car goes first, because it has no obstacle on its right. Once it has passed, the red car no longer has an obstacle on its right and so goes second. The blue car crosses the junction last, because it had an obstacle on its right — the red car.

question: Which car has stopped correctly on this two-way road while waiting for the green traffic light?
option_c: Both cars have stopped incorrectly.
explanation: The green car did not stop before the "Stop" line, and the white car is turning from the wrong lane (it is driving against the traffic).

question: Is it allowed to go straight ahead (there is a "250 m" plate under the sign)?
explanation: These road signs show that entry is prohibited 250 m further on, but that you may drive on for another 250 m.

question: Where must you stop?
option_b: At the edge of the junction (at point B).
option_c: Before the edge of the carriageway you are crossing (at point A).
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 204. Road sign "Stop". It is prohibited to proceed without stopping before the "Stop" line, or, if there is none, before the road sign.

question: What is marked by this distinguishing sign?
option_b: A motor vehicle, or a combination of vehicles, used for driving instruction.
option_c: A car with studded tyres.
option_d: A car driven by a deaf person.
explanation: Distinguishing sign 10. The front and the rear of motor vehicles and of combinations of vehicles with trailers used for driving instruction must be marked with a white equilateral triangle with a red border and a black letter "M" in the middle. The side of the triangle is 200–300 mm long and the width of the border is 1/10 of the length of the side.

question: In what order will the vehicles cross the junction if the police car has its beacons and siren switched on?
option_c: Yellow car, police car, motorcycle.
option_d: Motorcycle, yellow car, police car.

question: Do you have priority?
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 206. "Priority over oncoming traffic". A narrow section of road on which the driver travelling through it has priority over approaching oncoming traffic.

question: In this situation at 10 o'clock in the morning you, in the red car, may:
option_c: Go straight ahead.
option_d: Go straight ahead and turn left.
explanation: The driver may not turn left or make a U-turn, because at 10 o'clock the sign prohibiting the turn applies. Turning right is not allowed either, because the car is in the second lane of the carriageway. To turn right it would have to move into the first lane. Only going straight ahead is left.

question: The sign indicates:
option_b: Pedestrians are prohibited from walking on the side of the road where the sign is placed.
option_c: Only pedestrians may pass.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 310 "No pedestrians". Pedestrians are prohibited from walking on the side of the road where the sign is placed.

question: Which car will cross the junction third?
option_c: The cherry-red car.
option_d: The red car.
explanation: The cherry-red car goes first, because it is on the major road. The green car goes second: it will stop in the middle of the junction and move off only after letting the cherry-red car pass. The blue car then goes third (having let the cherry-red car pass), and finally the red car, because when turning left it must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction that are going straight ahead or turning right (the blue car).

question: Is the cyclist allowed to go straight ahead through the junction?
option_b: It is allowed, after letting the car pass.
explanation: The cyclist must give way, because the traffic light is red for them. A green arrow in an additional traffic light section allows movement only when there is nothing in the way. Where there is no shoulder, a cyclist is allowed to ride in the far right lane of the carriageway, keeping as close as possible to its right-hand edge.

question: Which road sign has the meaning "Vehicle ferry, port or landing stage"?
explanation: Road sign 732. "Vehicle ferry, port or landing stage". A floating bridge or a vessel used to carry vehicles across a sea, lake, river or other body of water. This sign may also mark a port or a landing stage.

question: In which case is it allowed to pass this road sign if your vehicle is higher than the height shown on it?
option_a: If you drive at a safe speed.
option_b: It is allowed only with a special permit.
option_c: It is not allowed in any case.
explanation: Getting a special permit does not make the vehicle smaller, nor does it make the obstacle higher. A safe speed will not get you past the obstacle either. If your vehicle is higher than the height shown on the sign, you may not proceed.

question: In what order should this junction be crossed?
explanation: Car No 1 crosses the junction first, because it is travelling on the major road and its path stays on the major road. Car No 2 goes second, because it is also leaving the major road. Vehicle No 3 must give way to both cars, because the road sign "Give way" applies to it and it is on the minor road: the driver must give way to vehicles travelling on the crossing or joining road and, where the supplementary plate No 843 "Direction of the major road" is used, to vehicles travelling on the major road.

question: Beyond the road sign shown:
option_a: Driving no faster than 70 km/h is allowed.
option_b: Driving no slower than 70 km/h is allowed.
option_c: The minimum speed restriction has ended.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 415. Road sign "End of minimum speed limit".

question: Which road sign prohibits a vehicle from standing on working days only?
option_c: No 3
option_d: No 4
explanation:
1. Road sign 333 — No standing.
2. Road sign 334 — No standing on odd days.
3. Road sign 335 — No standing on even days.
4. Road sign 333 — No standing, together with plate 823 — Working days.
5. Road sign 333 — No standing, together with plate 822 — Non-working days.

question: Overtaking is prohibited:
option_b: For all vehicles, of all vehicles, except single vehicles travelling at less than 30 km/h.
option_c: Only of cars and lorries with a maximum authorised mass below 3.5 tonnes.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 325 "No overtaking". It is prohibited to overtake moving vehicles, except single vehicles (or single combinations of vehicles) travelling at less than 30 km/h.

question: May you turn into the road on the right after seeing this road sign?
explanation: This sign shows the direction of the major road at a place with limited visibility, but it does not prohibit turning the other way if there is a road there.

question: Which vehicles are allowed to stand in the parking space marked by this road sign?
option_a: Vehicles marked with the "Disabled person" distinguishing sign.
option_c: Vehicles serving premises in the area.
option_d: Scheduled public transport.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 531. "Reserved parking space". A parking space where vehicles may stand only with special permits. Permits that are not electronic are displayed behind the windscreen.

question: Is it allowed to turn left in this situation if you are driving a car with a trailer?
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 307. No vehicles with trailers (it is prohibited to drive cars, tractors and self-propelled machines with trailers).

question: The driver of a car is reversing. Who has priority in this situation?
explanation: In this situation it does not matter that the person is not using a crossing and is therefore breaking the rules. When reversing, the driver must give way to all other road users, even those who are breaking the rules.

question: What do these road signs indicate?
option_a: You are approaching on a minor road a junction beyond which the one-way street ends.
option_b: You are approaching on a minor road a junction beyond which a one-way street begins.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules clauses:
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 203. "Give way". The driver must give way to vehicles travelling on the crossing road.
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 504. "End of one-way street".

question: Which vehicle is breaking the rules?
option_a: The driver of the first car.
option_b: The driver of the second car.
option_c: Both cars are standing correctly.
option_d: Both cars are standing incorrectly.
explanation: When stopping or standing beside a solid line, at least 3 m must be left up to that line. Car 2 has left only 2.5 m and is therefore breaking the rules. Car 1 has left 2 m up to the edge of the carriageway, so it is not breaking the rules.

question: What path does a trailer follow when a bus goes round a bend?
option_a: It moves towards the outside of the bend.
option_b: It follows the same path as the bus.
option_c: It moves towards the inside of the bend.
option_d: It moves towards the inside of the bend only at high speed.
explanation: When going round a bend, the trailer's wheels always follow a smaller radius than the bus's wheels. You can see this from the tracks left by the wheels of the bus and the trailer when going round a bend on a carriageway that is covered in snow or is wet.

question: What should you do in this situation?
option_a: Reduce speed and let the bus driver complete the manoeuvre.
option_b: The bus driver is prohibited from entering the oncoming lane.
option_c: Pass the bus by driving on the pavement.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules, clause 107. Where, because of its size or for other reasons, a vehicle cannot turn (or turn round) from the outermost position, turning is also allowed from a position other than the corresponding edge of the carriageway used for that direction, provided that this will not obstruct other vehicles and will not endanger other road users.
Road Traffic Rules, clause 125. Vehicles (except bicycles and electric micromobility vehicles) are prohibited from passing vehicles travelling in the same direction on their right (except for the permitted passing on the right of vehicles that are turning left or making a U-turn) while driving on the shoulder or in a deceleration or acceleration lane. Slower vehicles travelling in the same direction should be passed on the left.

question: Which road sign prohibits turning left (if you are not driving scheduled public transport)?
option_c: No 3.
option_d: No 4.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 527. Road sign "Turning place". A place for turning round away from a junction.
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 404. Road sign "Ahead or right only". Movement is allowed only in the directions of the arrows. The sign applies at the carriageway intersection before which it is placed. Its requirements do not apply to scheduled public transport.
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 324. Road sign "No U-turns". It does not apply to scheduled public transport and does not prohibit turning left.
Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 146. Road sign "Direction of bend to the right". The direction of travel on a bend of small radius with limited visibility, at a narrowing of the road, or at a place where the road is being repaired or built.

question: What does this road sign indicate?
option_a: An additional lane, or the start of a deceleration lane.
option_b: The directions of traffic at a junction.
option_c: A road with two lanes.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 513. Road sign "Lane begins on the right". An additional lane, or the start of a deceleration lane. Vehicles leaving the road must move into the deceleration lane; vehicles going uphill that cannot travel faster than those behind them must move into the additional lane.

question: In a built-up area a driver will not breach the requirement of this sign by driving:
option_a: At 50 km/h as far as the nearest junction.
option_b: At 50 km/h beyond the nearest junction.
option_c: At no more than 40 km/h both as far as the nearest junction and beyond it.
explanation: This is because the sign applies not just as far as the first junction, but throughout the area beyond it until there are road signs cancelling the restriction.

question: What is the name of the road sign shown?
option_c: Junction with a minor road.
explanation: Road Traffic Rules, Annex 1, sign 203. Give way (the driver must give way to vehicles travelling on the crossing or joining road and, where the supplementary plate No 843 "Direction of the major road" is used, to vehicles travelling on the major road).

question: Which car will cross the junction first (the traffic light next to the green car has an additional plate with a green arrow to the right that is not lit, and the red light is showing)?
explanation:
Explanation:
The driver of the blue car has priority, because they are moving on a permitting signal from the additional traffic light section. The driver of the green car must give way to the blue car, because they are moving under the additional plate with the green arrow and have no priority.

question: The vehicle ahead of you is signalling a right turn as it approaches a junction with a minor road, but it does not turn. What will you do?
option_c: Pass it on the right.
option_d: Slow down and carry on behind the car.
explanation:
Road Traffic Rules, clause 4. The behaviour of road users is based on mutual respect and caution.
Road Traffic Rules, clause 9. Road users must take all necessary precautions, must not endanger the safety of other road users, of other people or of their property or the environment, must not obstruct their movement, and, in order to avoid or reduce harmful consequences, must take all necessary measures, except where this would endanger their own life or health or that of others, or where such measures would cause even more harm than could be avoided.

question: While driving, two of your wheels have gone onto the shoulder. What should you do?
option_a: Without braking, turn the steering wheel sharply and return to the carriageway.
option_b: Reduce speed gently and turn the steering wheel slowly, bringing the car back onto the carriageway.
option_c: Stop and then move off again.
explanation: In such a case the car should be brought back onto the carriageway calmly, without braking and by turning the steering wheel slowly. Turning the wheel sharply can be dangerous, because the increased sideways force may make the car start to skid or even roll over. You should also avoid braking sharply, because the wheels on the gravel grip the road less well than the wheels on the asphalt. Because of this difference in grip the car may become unstable and leave its path.

question: What will you do if the road signs contradict the road marking lines?
option_a: I will follow the road signs.
option_b: I will follow the road marking lines.
